ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Here is a Physoly round button badge, in which the logo is printed on the flat and rigid surface of this badge. Toss it in the air and track the motions of three points (indicated by cyan circles in the figure) separated a straight-line distance of $L=5 \mathrm{~mm}$ apart. At a particular moment, we find that these all have the same speed $V=4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$ but are heading to different directions which form an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$ between each pair. Determine the then angular velocity of the badge (in $\left.\mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\right)$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a circular, flat white badge/disc, with a colored Physoly-style pattern printed on its surface. Near the center of the pattern there are three fixed points marked with small cyan circles, and these points are located on the rigid printed surface. Reasoning: Choose any two cyan marked points. The problem gives that the straight-line distance between these two points is L = 5 mm, and at that instant the magnitudes of their velocities are both V = 4 cm/s, with the angle between the velocity directions being θ = 30°. The magnitude of the difference between two equal-length velocity vectors is obtained from the law of cosines as |v_i - v_j| = sqrt(V^2 + V^2 - 2V^2 cosθ) = 2V sin(θ/2). For the badge undergoing planar rigid-body motion, the magnitude of the relative velocity between two points satisfies |v_i - v_j| = ωL. Therefore ω = 2V sin(θ/2)/L. Substituting V = 0.04 m/s, L = 0.005 m, θ/2 = 15°, gives ω = 2(0.04)sin15°/0.005 = 4.1411 rad/s.

Compute the magnitude of their relative velocity by the cosine rule on the two equal velocity vectors: |v_i - v_j| = sqrt(V^2 + V^2 - 2V^2 cos theta) = 2V sin(theta/2). For a rigid badge undergoing planar rotation, the relative speed of two points separated by L is |v_i - v_j| = omega L.
